# Registry reference

One section per registry: merge semantics, the `Data` table the merge
writes, and the value schema. Where Gold differs -- a different table, a
different record, or no home at all -- the registry carries a Gen 2
subsection built from the same catalog entry. Concepts and verbs:
[Concepts: Registries](Concepts-Registries).

## Reading this reference

Use the wiki's `Choose-A-Registry` guide when you know what you want
to make but not the registry name. This page is the precise schema
catalog once you have chosen one.

### Type notation

- `string`, `number`, `boolean`, and `function` name the Lua value to
  supply. A function is code the engine calls later; see the linked
  concept/reference page for its arguments and return value.
- `{ field, otherField? }` is a record (a Lua table with named fields).
  A `?` means that field is optional. `list of T` is an ordered Lua
  table of values shaped like `T`; `map of K -> V` maps each key to a
  value shaped like `V`.
- `A | B` means either shape is accepted. `moves id`, `items id`, and
  similar phrases mean the internal id of a record in that registry,
  not its displayed name.

### Example status

Every example below is **shape only**. Put an adapted call in your mod
entry file. Replace `...` and names such as `fn` with real values, and
supply every field marked required when registering a new record.

### On Gen 3

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.gen3BattleAnims`

The record differs; the registry name, the verbs and the id space
do not.
- value: {seq, source?}

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.battle_anims:register("SHADOW_BALL", { seq = { { op = "createvisualtask", task = "AnimTask_ShakeMon", priority = 2, args = { "target", 3, 0, 6, 1 } }, { op = "waitforvisualfinish" }, { op = "end" } } })
```

On Gen 3 the id is a move id and `seq` is the battle animation script the cart runs for it: rows of the same `op` vocabulary the ROM pack uses (createsprite, createvisualtask, delay, playsewithpan, waitforvisualfinish, end). A native move id replaces its animation. Gen 1 subanimation and tilesheet records do not exist on Gen 3.

## battle_sprite_scales

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.battle_sprite_scales`

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | file path | yes |
| `scale` | number 0.25..4 | yes |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.battle_sprite_scales:register("abra_back", {
  path = "assets/generated/battle/back/abrab.png",
  scale = 1.5,
})
```

Scales one battle pic by its asset path, overriding the species-level
`battleScaleFront`/`battleScaleBack` (see [pokemon](#pokemon)) for that
image. The only way to scale a pic that is not species-keyed, like the
player's trainer back sprite. Resolution order at draw time:
image-level, then species-level, then the defaults (1x front, 2x back).
The pic stays grounded at any scale: player feet stay flush on the
text-box top, the enemy pic stays bottom-pinned in its slot, and the
scale composes with the send-out grow animation.

### On Gen 3

Not available on Gen 3: there is no native target for this registry.
A write here is dropped and reported on a Gen 3 boot.

### On Gen 3

- semantics: `record`
- target on `emerald`, `ruby`, `sapphire`: `Data.gen3Decorations`

Not available on the other Gen 3 versions: a write there is
dropped and reported.

The record differs; the registry name, the verbs and the id space
do not.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `category` | integer 0..7 | yes |
| `description` | string | yes |
| `id` | string | no |
| `index` | integer 1..255 | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `permission` | integer 0..3 | yes |
| `price` | integer 0..65535 | yes |
| `shape` | integer 0..9 | yes |
| `tiles` | list of integer 0..1023 | yes |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.decorations:register("DECOR_MOD_DESK", { name = "MOD DESK", index = 130, permission = 0, shape = 0, category = 0, price = 500, description = "A desk.", tiles = { 640 } })
```

A Gen 3 decoration is a gDecorations row (Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald only). `index` is the decoration id the bag, the secret base save and scripts use; an id the cart already has replaces that row. `permission` is DECORPERM_SOLID_FLOOR..NA_WALL (0..3: sprite decorations are not moddable), `shape` DECORSHAPE_*, `category` DECORCAT_*, and `tiles` the metatile ids painted row by row.

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.encounters`

| field | type | required |

### On Gold (Gen 2)

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.gen2Encounters`

The record differs; the registry name, the verbs and the id space
do not.

Id = a top-level key of the target table. The set below is **closed**:
an id that is not one of these is rejected rather than merged, because
the engine reads this table by name and a key it does not name is a
write nothing reads.

| key | type |
|---|---|
| `bugContest` | list of {chance, max, min, species} |
| `fishGroups` | map of string -> {chance, good, id?, index?, old, super} |
| `generation` | integer >= 1 |
| `grass` | map of string -> {map?, rates, slots} |
| `roamMaps` | list of {map, to} |
| `roamMons` | list of {level?, map?, mapGroup?, mapNumber?, species?} |
| `rocks` | map of string -> string |
| `source` | string |
| `swarmGrass` | map of string -> {map?, rates, slots} |
| `swarmWater` | map of string -> {map?, rate, slots} |
| `timeFishGroups` | map of string \| integer 0..255 -> {day, nite} |
| `treeMonsAsleep` | {DAY, MORN, NITE} |
| `treeSets` | map of string -> {common, rare?} |
| `trees` | map of string -> string |
| `water` | map of string -> {map?, rate, slots} |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.encounters:patch("grass", { ROUTE_29 = { rates = { NITE = 40 } } })
```

Gold's encounter ids are a **closed set**: the kinds above are
the complete set of lookups the engine makes into `Data.gen2Encounters`, so an
id that is not one of them is a write nothing reads. An id outside the set is
rejected -- a Gen 1 mod ported unchanged passes the map where Gold wants the
kind, and that call is refused rather than silently dropped.

## field

- semantics: `deep`
- target: `Data.field`

Id = a top-level key of the target table. Keys not listed here are
accepted and merged as-is.

| key | type |
|---|---|
| `badgeGates` | map of string -> {badge?, coords?, failText?, guards?, passText?, passedFlag?, text?} |
| `boot` | {lastHeal?, namePresets?, playerName?, rivalName?, screens?, startFacing?, startMap?, startMoney?, startX?, startY?, starterScript?, title?} |
| `flyOrder` | list of string |
| `hiddenItems` | map of string -> list of {item, x, y} |
| `ledges` | list of {facing, input, ledgeTile, standingTile, tileset?} |
| `playerPics` | {back?, demoBack?, front?, oakBack?} |
| `townMap` | {background?, cursorOrder?, gridPixelSize?, locations?, nest?, upArrow?} |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.field:patch("boot", { startMap = "SABLE_COVE" })
```

### On Gold (Gen 2)

- semantics: `deep`
- target: `Data.field`

The record differs; the registry name, the verbs and the id space
do not.

Id = a top-level key of the target table. The set below is **closed**:
an id that is not one of these is rejected rather than merged, because
the engine reads this table by name and a key it does not name is a
write nothing reads.

| key | type |
|---|---|
| `boot` | {namePresets?, rivalName?, startFacing?, startMap?, startMoney?, startX?, startY?} |
| `emotes` | {bolt?, cutGrass?, fish?, fishing?, fishingFemale?, grassRustle?, happy?, heart?, jumpShadow?, order?, question?, sad?, shock?, sleep?} |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.field:patch("boot", { startMap = "NEW_BARK_TOWN", startX = 6, startY = 8 })
```

Gold reads `boot` and `emotes`. `boot` is the New Game spawn (`startMap`, `startX`, `startY`, `startFacing`, replacing SPAWN_HOME), the starting money, the rival's starting name and the naming presets. `emotes` is the overworld emote art, one image path per sheet: the showemote bubbles listed in `order`, `grassRustle`, `jumpShadow`, `cutGrass`, the fishing pose `fishing` and Crystal's `fishingFemale`; a patched path is the sheet the overworld draws. Every other Gen 1 key has no Gold consumer: `ledges` (Gold's ledges are tile collision types), `hiddenItems` (bg events in `maps`), `badgeGates`, `townMap` (`landmarks`), `flyOrder` (the flypoint table), `playerPics`, and `boot.lastHeal`, `boot.screens`, `boot.starterScript`, `boot.title`, `boot.playerName`.

### On Gen 3

Not available on Gen 3: there is no native target for this registry.
A write here is dropped and reported on a Gen 3 boot.

## fly_points

- semantics: `record`
- target: none

Gen 2 only: Red, Blue and Yellow have no native target for this registry.
A write here on a Gen 1 boot is dropped
and reported. See the Gold subsection below for where it does land.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `flag` | integer 0..65535 | no |
| `landmark` | landmarks id | yes |
| `order` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `region` | one of "johto" \| "kanto" | yes |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.fly_points:register("SPAWN_MOD_TOWN", { landmark = "LANDMARK_MOD_TOWN", region = "johto", order = 3 })
```

Gen 2 only. The id is the SPAWN_* row (see `spawns`) the point lands on; a row whose spawn is missing is dropped. `order` places it in its region's cursor order (the cart's rows are 0..23); a row without one sorts after them by id. Without `flag` the point counts as visited the first time the player enters the spawn's map; with `flag` (an engine flag id of 256 or more that no other row claims) the mod's map script sets it. A cart row keeps its own flag. Kanto rows appear only once SPAWN_INDIGO is visited, as on the cart.

### On Gold (Gen 2)

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.gen2Landmarks.flypoints`

### On Gen 3

Not available on Gen 3: there is no native target for this registry.
A write here is dropped and reported on a Gen 3 boot.

### On Gold (Gen 2)

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `ball` | balls id | no |
| `effect` | item_effects id | no |
| `id` | string | yes |

New records receive an unused script index above the native range, up to 65535. Existing indices cannot change; collisions and reserved species 253, move 255 and item 255 are rejected. Cartridge save export refuses named records whose index exceeds one byte.

## landmarks

- semantics: `record`
- target: none

Gen 2 only: Red, Blue and Yellow have no native target for this registry.
A write here on a Gen 1 boot is dropped
and reported. See the Gold subsection below for where it does land.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | no |
| `index` | integer >= 0 | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `x` | integer -8..247 | yes |
| `y` | integer -16..239 | yes |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.landmarks:patch("LANDMARK_ROUTE_29", { x = 12 })
```

### On Gold (Gen 2)

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.gen2Landmarks.landmarks`

### On Gen 3

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.gen3Landmarks`

The record differs; the registry name, the verbs and the id space
do not.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | integer >= 1 | no |
| `id` | string | no |
| `index` | integer 0..255 | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `region` | integer 0..3 | no |
| `theme` | one of "wood" \| "marble" \| "stone" \| "brick" \| "underwater" \| "stone2" | no |
| `width` | integer >= 1 | no |
| `x` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `y` | integer >= 0 | no |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.landmarks:register("MAPSEC_MOD_COVE", { name = "MOD COVE", index = 230, theme = "wood", x = 4, y = 6 })
```

A Gen 3 landmark is a map section (the byte a map header carries as `regionMapSectionId`). `index` names the section: an index the cart already uses renames and re-themes it, a free one adds a new section. `x`/`y` (and `width`/`height`, default 1) are zero-based region map cells the cursor resolves to this section; `region` picks the FireRed region layout (0 Kanto, 1..3 Sevii) and Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald ignore it. The pretty tilemap art is not redrawn.

### On Gen 3

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.maps`

The record differs; the registry name, the verbs and the id space
do not.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `allowEscaping` | integer 0..1 | no |
| `allowRunning` | integer 0..1 | no |
| `battleType` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `bikingAllowed` | integer 0..1 | no |
| `blocks` | list of integer 0..65535 \| {collision?, elevation?, metatile} | no |
| `border` | list of integer 0..1023 | no |
| `borderHeight` | integer 1..255 | no |
| `borderWidth` | integer 1..255 | no |
| `cave` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `cells` | list of {collision?, elevation?, metatile, x, y} | no |
| `connections` | any value | no |
| `floorNum` | integer | no |
| `height` | integer >= 1 | no |
| `id` | string | no |
| `mapType` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `music` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `name` | string | no |
| `objects` | list of any value | no |
| `pair` | string | no |
| `regionMapSectionId` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `showMapName` | integer 0..1 | no |
| `tileset` | any value | no |
| `warps` | list of any value | no |
| `weather` | integer >= 0 | no |
| `width` | integer >= 1 | no |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.maps:patch("FR_PALLET_TOWN", { weather = 2 })
```

`blocks` is a full row-major grid of width*height pret map.bin words (metatile | collision << 10 | elevation << 12) or { metatile, collision?, elevation? } records. A register or override with `blocks` needs width, height and `pair` copied from an existing map (`maps:get("FR_VIRIDIAN_FOREST").pair`), and a new id given `blocks` must keep the game's prefix (FR_, EM_, ...). A `blocks` patch on an existing map keeps its width, height, pair and border unless the patch gives them. A map registered without `blocks` gets no grid from the mod and is drawn only when the cache already holds a layout for that id; neither its grid nor its id prefix is checked. `cells` patches single map cells ({ x, y, metatile, collision?, elevation? }); an omitted collision is passable and an omitted elevation keeps the cell's own, so emit collision for blocked cells. A patch repaints one map id only, even where the cartridge shares the layout. `border` lists metatile ids (1x1 by default on FireRed and LeafGreen, always 2x2 on Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald). Patching an id no map has is an error. When a mod's `blocks`, `cells` or `border` are invalid, only that mod's layout writes to that map are dropped. Example: mod.content.maps:patch("FR_ROUTE_1", { cells = { { x = 10, y = 5, metatile = 0x00D, collision = 1 } } })

## spawns

- semantics: `record`
- target: none

Gen 2 only: Red, Blue and Yellow have no native target for this registry.
A write here on a Gen 1 boot is dropped
and reported. See the Gold subsection below for where it does land.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | no |
| `index` | integer 0..255 | no |
| `map` | maps id | yes |
| `x` | integer 0..255 | yes |
| `y` | integer 0..255 | yes |

<!-- snippet: illustrative -->
```lua
mod.content.spawns:patch("SPAWN_VIOLET", { x = 30 })
```

Gen 2 only. Ids are SPAWN_* names. `map` is the OUTDOOR map a town's Pokemon Center is entered from, and `x`/`y` the cell a Fly or a whiteout lands on there; walking from that map into a Pokemon Center makes the row the whiteout point. `index` is the cart's SPAWN_* byte; a registered row has none and is never written to a .sav.

### On Gold (Gen 2)

- semantics: `record`
- target: `Data.gen2Landmarks.spawns`

### On Gen 3

Not available on Gen 3: there is no native target for this registry.
A write here is dropped and reported on a Gen 3 boot.
